P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes, but under strict exchange control. Every exporter of goods and every service provider under ordinary law must sell 70% of its export receipts on the foreign-exchange market upon repatriation, within 30 days at most. After that, local banks must sell the currency on the next working day at the best rate.

sources.publisher: Décret n° 2022-1183 (Code des changes / réglementation des changes) — cnlegis.gov.mg
sources.title: Décret 2022-1183 — cession des recettes d'exportation

P1_fx_receipts.notes: TRAP: applies to service providers too (prestataire de services) - a freelancer billing abroad may have to convert 70%. Whether individuals are 'prestataires régis par le droit commun' in practice not confirmed.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes, regulated. Foreign-currency accounts can be funded by transfers received directly from abroad. Transfers between residents' FX accounts are not allowed except in listed cases (e.g. between accounts of the same holder). Holders may carry out current operations directly related to their activities.

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Madagascar (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest: an individual enterprise (EI), with no minimum capital and unlimited liability. Registration goes through the EDBM one-stop shop (Economic Development Board of Madagascar) / RCS, plus a NIF and a statistical number (INSTAT). Fees and timelines were not confirmed officially.

L2_tax_id.answer: A NIF (Numéro d'Identification Fiscale) from the DGI is mandatory; a guide says it is free and takes 2–3 days (NIFONLINE application). A statistical number from INSTAT is also required.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: An individual business with annual turnover under MGA 400 million pays the 'synthetic tax' (impôt synthétique): 5% of turnover, with a possible 70% reduction (PwC). Taxpayers between MGA 200m and 400m may opt for the real income-tax regime (IR) without VAT; the option was reinstated by the 2026 Finance Act and requires certified financial statements. For salary tax (IRSA), residents are taxed on worldwide income; non-residents pay IR only on Malagasy-source income.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 20%, and exports are 0%. VAT applies to businesses with turnover of MGA 400 million or more. Those between MGA 200m and 400m may opt for IR without VAT (L3). Whether exported services qualify for 0% was not confirmed.

L4_vat_gst.notes: PwC's MGA 400m sentence refers to 'corporate entity'; threshold for individuals assumed the same (consistent with the synthetic tax ceiling).

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Law 2014-038 on personal data protection exists, but per DLA Piper it is not yet effectively applied, as no implementing decree has been published. The CMIL authority was created by Decree 2023-1541 but is not fully operational until all members are appointed (MoFo: not yet established). On paper, processing requires prior declaration to the CMIL.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
